headline: TUDOR GOLD PERFECTSTORM: DUAL SYSTEM CONFIRMED — New Copper-Gold Porphyry (0.21% Cu Over 82.9m) + Epithermal (0.78 g/t Over 74m) In Golden Triangle BC
snippet: Tudor Gold Corp. (TSX-V: TUD) reported August 6, 2026 that the first four holes of its 2026 Treaty Creek drill program have simultaneously identified two distinct systems at the Perfectstorm Zone in BC's Golden Triangle: a new copper-gold-silver-molybdenum porphyry (the PSP Zone), with highlight hole PS-26-15 returning 82.90 metres at 0.21% copper, 0.24 g/t Au, 2.11 g/t Ag and 50.76 ppm molybdenum, and a gold-silver epithermal system (PSE Zone) confirmed over at least 360 metres of strike with PS-26-17 returning 74.15 metres at 0.78 g/t Au and 2.90 g/t Ag. Treaty Creek hosts the GoldStorm deposit — one of BC's largest undeveloped gold-copper systems — making the Perfectstorm dual-system discovery a meaningful potential expansion adjacent to the primary asset, with two drills now advancing both zones.

headline: OSISKO GOLD HITS 95.93 g/t AU OVER 4.6m AT PROSERPINE — New Open Pit System 1km x 500m At Cariboo Regional Ground; Open In All Directions
snippet: Osisko Gold Group Inc. confirmed August 5 that 14 diamond drill holes (6,463 metres) at the Proserpine Target on the Cariboo Gold Project's regional property in British Columbia have outlined a new mineralized system with open pit potential, with standout hole PSP-26-004 returning 4.60 metres at 95.93 g/t gold from 110 metres depth — including a 50-centimetre interval at 873 g/t Au — and hole PSP-26-001 returning 8.60 metres at 5.46 g/t Au. The mineralized footprint now spans approximately 1 kilometre along strike by 500 metres in width with all four sides open, adding a potential open-pit satellite to Cariboo's planned underground mine; OGG shares rallied on the news.

headline: ENERGY FUELS CALLS Q2 'TRANSFORMATIONAL' — $996M Working Capital, 740K lbs U3O8 H1; Tb-Dy Rare Earth Circuits By 2027; ASM Acquisition Advancing (NYSE: UUUU)
snippet: Energy Fuels Inc. (NYSE: UUUU) reported Q2 2026 results on August 5, describing the period as 'transformational' as it simultaneously mines uranium, builds rare earth processing capacity, and advances the acquisition of ASM (Australia Strategic Materials Ltd.). Uranium production totalled 740,000 pounds U3O8 in H1 2026 across Pinyon Plain, La Sal and Pandora mines, with full-year guidance on track; working capital stood at $996 million as of June 30 ($58.4M cash plus $878.3M in marketable securities). The company's White Mesa Mill in Utah is being expanded with terbium and dysprosium separation circuits targeted for completion by end-2027, followed by samarium, europium and gadolinium by 2028 — positioning Energy Fuels as the only Western company on a technical path to commercial-scale separated heavy rare earth oxide production integrated with uranium processing.

headline: GRID METALS MAIDEN CESIUM + LITHIUM MRE COMMISSIONED — 14% Cs2O Peak At Lucy South; C$3.75M Avenir JV Closed; Fall 2026 Results (CVE: GRDM)
snippet: Grid Metals Corp. (TSX-V: GRDM) announced August 6, 2026 that SGS Canada Inc. has been engaged to prepare a maiden NI 43-101 mineral resource estimate for the Lucy South pollucite-cesium-lithium pegmatite at its Falcon West Property in southeastern Manitoba, alongside final Phase 2 drill assays that include individual samples reaching 27.4% Cs2O. The company also confirmed that Avenir Minerals has acquired a 15% JV stake in Falcon West for C$3.75 million, with TSX Venture Exchange approval received July 31. Cesium — used in atomic clocks underpinning GPS infrastructure, cesium formate drilling fluids, and emerging quantum computing applications — is not currently produced from any Canadian mine, and Lucy South's pollucite-rich zone represents a potentially strategic Western-hemisphere critical minerals asset ahead of its maiden resource estimate this fall.

headline: CRITICAL ELEMENTS ROSE WEST DRILL RESUMES POST-FIRE — Footprint Expands 6x To 1,250m x 800m; 10,000m Phase 2 Targets Fall MRE (CVE: CRE)
snippet: Critical Elements Lithium Corporation (TSX-V: CRE) announced August 4, 2026 that its Phase 2 summer drill program has resumed at the Rose West Discovery in Eeyou Istchee, Quebec, following a temporary suspension caused by a nearby forest fire in July — all personnel returned safely after conditions cleared. The 10,000-metre program targets three newly identified lithium-tantalum-bearing pegmatites intersected during the Winter 2026 campaign, with a mineral resource estimate targeted for Q4 2026. The known mineralised pegmatite footprint at Rose West has expanded from 450 metres x 370 metres (first intersected in Winter 2024) to 1,250 metres x 800 metres today — a six-fold areal increase — located 10 kilometres west of Critical Elements' established Rose Lithium-Tantalum Project in Quebec's active James Bay lithium belt.

headline: F4 URANIUM: FIRST SURVEY NEXT TO ARROW + TRIPLE R — Same Method That Located Triple R Boulder Train; 3,850 Line-km SW Athabasca (TSX-V: FFU)
source_name: Globe and Mail / F4 Uranium Corp.
snippet: F4 Uranium Corp. (TSX-V: FFU) announced August 4 that RAMP Geological Services has commenced the first-ever high-resolution airborne radiometric survey over its 100%-owned Todd Lake and Wales Lake Projects in Saskatchewan's southwestern Athabasca Basin, covering 3,850 line kilometres. The survey uses the same RAMP-HD helicopter-borne radiometric system that identified the Patterson Lake South radioactive boulder train — the discovery that ultimately led to Paladin Energy's Triple R Deposit, located 13 kilometres east of Todd Lake. Todd and Wales Lake sit immediately west of NexGen Energy's Arrow Deposit and Paladin Energy's Triple R — the two highest-grade uranium discoveries in the Athabasca Basin in the past decade — making F4's maiden radiometric survey a high-priority early-stage watch for uranium sector investors.

headline: TRACTION URANIUM AURORA: MULTIPLE RADIOMETRIC ANOMALIES CONFIRMED — Ground Follow-Up Planned; Athabasca Basin (TSX-V: TRAC / CSE: COSA)
snippet: Traction Uranium Corp. (TSX-V: TRAC) reported August 4 that a partner-funded airborne radiometric survey over Cosa Resources' (CSE: COSA) Aurora Uranium Project in the Athabasca Basin has returned multiple radiometric anomalies — the first formal geophysical targets generated at the project. Traction funded the survey as part of its option/earn-in arrangement with Cosa on the Aurora project. Radiometric anomalies in the southwestern Athabasca Basin have a strong historical track record as early-stage discovery indicators: uranium deposits in the region are typically associated with structural conduits identifiable through elevated surface radioactivity before drilling confirms depth mineralisation. Ground follow-up, including prospecting and drill target prioritisation, is the next planned step.

headline: RUA GOLD APPROVED TO DRILL NZ HAURAKI GOLDFIELD — Adjacent To 1.5 Moz At 17.3 g/t Au; 9,000m Program Launches Q4 2026 (TSX: RUA)
snippet: Rua Gold Inc. (TSX: RUA) received regulatory approval on August 4, 2026 to commence exploration drilling at the Glamorgan Project in New Zealand's Hauraki Goldfield — home to over 50 historic mines that collectively produced more than 15 million ounces of gold. The Glamorgan Project is directly adjacent to OceanaGold's Wharekirauponga deposit, which hosts Indicated Mineral Resources of 1.5 million ounces at 17.3 g/t gold, one of the highest-grade undeveloped epithermal systems in the Pacific region. A fully funded initial 9,000-metre drill program is planned across Glamorgan's targets with drilling expected to commence in Q4 2026, making Rua Gold's Hauraki ground one of the most compelling high-grade adjacency plays in Southern Hemisphere gold exploration.

headline: SILVER HITS HIGHEST SINCE JUNE 22 — Opens At $62.20 On Aug 6; ADP Miss + Hormuz Progress Drive 4% Jump From Wednesday's Open
snippet: Silver September futures opened at $62.20 per ounce on Thursday August 6, 2026 — their highest level since June 22 — extending Wednesday's 5.38% surge as the macro catalysts driving gold's seven-week high continued to benefit silver: the ADP employment miss (44K vs. 70K forecast), the Iran-Oman Strait of Hormuz partial shipping corridor deal, and a weakening US dollar. Silver sits approximately 10% above its late-July lows and is well above the $60 floor that analysts had identified as critical for the bull trend's integrity; with Non-Farm Payrolls due Friday, a soft employment print could drive silver toward the $65 resistance zone it last visited before this summer's consolidation, while a hot print above 150K jobs would likely erase much of the week's gains.

headline: COPPER HOLDS NEAR RECORD AT $6.71/LB — Bull Trend Intact Despite Daily Dip; +53% Year-On-Year As 200K+ Tonnes Remain In US Ports
snippet: Copper eased to $6.71 per pound on August 6, 2026 — down 0.28% on the day after hitting a COMEX all-time high of $6.7045/lb ($14,781/tonne) on August 5 — but analysts say the structural bull trend remains firmly intact: copper is up 53% year-on-year, with more than 200,000 tonnes arriving at US ports in July alone as importers front-run the 2027 tariff phase-in. The COMEX/LME price spread remains historically wide, reflecting the bifurcation between tariff-driven US demand and softer ex-US pricing; for junior copper developers priced against LME, the sustained COMEX premium is real-time validation of the supply deficit thesis that underpins NAV models across the TSX-V and ASX copper developer space.
